# Centralized FRC Pit Operations Application

System Requirements & Architecture Document

# 1\. Executive Summary

During FIRST Robotics Competition (FRC) events, the pit environment is subject to high strain, time constraints, noise, and intense pressure. The Pit Operations Application serves as a mission-control interface for pit crew leads, drive team members, mechanical/controls specialists, and strategy personnel.

The primary objective is to streamline turnaround times between matches, reduce human error in robot preparation, maintain real-time health visibility, and seamlessly sync operational status with the strategy and scouting teams.

---

# 2\. Event & Pit Operations Management

The application shall provide a centralized view of the team's operational status throughout the entire FRC event. The system shall distinguish between **official event schedule information**, **team-specific operational milestones**, and **real-time robot/pit status**.

## 2.1 General Event Timeline

The application shall maintain a chronological event timeline covering the complete lifecycle of an FRC event, not just individual matches.

### 2.1.1 Standard Event Milestones

The system shall be configurable and support, at minimum, the following event milestones:

**Event Preparation**

* Team arrival / pit load-in  
* Pit setup  
* Robot modifications  
* Robot power-on / initial systems check  
* Radio/network setup  
* Inspection preparation  
* Robot inspection  
* Field calibration  
* Practice field opening  
* Practice schedule

**Competition Day**

* Leaving hotel for event  
* Pit opening  
* Driver meeting  
* Practice matches  
* Opening ceremonies  
* Qualification matches  
* Lunch / scheduled event breaks  
* Leaving event for hotel  
* Qualification matches complete  
* Reinspection after qualification matches  
* Alliance Selection  
* Dinner  
* Hotel general meeting, pit meeting

**Elimination Tournament**

* Alliance Selection  
* Elimination rounds  
* Event awards  
* Closing ceremonies

**Event Closeout**

* Pit teardown  
* Pit load-out  
* Departure

The application shall allow event-specific milestones to be added, removed, renamed, or reordered without requiring a software update.

### 2.1.2 Event Timeline Display

The event timeline shall be displayed in two locations. On an overview page, it shall show a few hours around the current time with the ability to scroll. On a schedule page, it shall show the entire schedule in one view with configurable toggles for different types of events. 

### 2.1.3 Event Schedule Changes

Because FRC event schedules may run ahead of or behind the published schedule, the system shall distinguish between:

* Published match time  
* Estimated actual match time  
* Actual match start time  
* Actual match completion time

The system shall automatically recalculate downstream operational timers when sufficient schedule information is available.

A user shall be able to manually override the estimated schedule when official timing information is unavailable or inaccurate.

### 2.1.4 Team Operational Timeline

In addition to the official event schedule, the application shall support team-created operational events such as:

* Replace drivetrain module  
* Perform robot inspection  
* Swap battery  
* Repair subsystem  
* Run automated robot test  
* Perform driver practice  
* Recalibrate sensors  
* Prepare robot for queue  
* Begin post-match inspection

These events shall be recorded with timestamps and, where appropriate, linked to the associated match, robot test, maintenance record, or checklist. The check list based events shall record the timestamp of start and completion of the task for post competition review.

---

## 2.2 Schedule Dashboard

The application shall provide a dedicated Schedule dashboard showing all events. This should emulate common calendar programs such as google or microsoft calendars and show all of the days we are at the event (3 days). The current time should be shown with a horizontal line that traverses the calendar day.

---

# 3\. Robot Diagnostics & Network Ingestion

The Robot Diagnostics subsystem shall provide two complementary diagnostic modes:

1. **Live View** — monitor the robot while it is connected and operating.  
2. **Log Review** — review historical robot behavior after a match or test.

All three modes shall use a common metric and visualization framework so that the same data can be viewed live, historically, or as part of an automated test.

---

## 3.1 Local Network Auto-Discovery & Ingestion

When the robot is connected to the pit network, the application shall automatically discover available robot systems.

Discovery shall support mDNS and other configurable local-network discovery mechanisms.

### Automated Log Offloading

The application shall automatically identify and retrieve available diagnostic data, including:

* Driver Station logs  
* Driver Station event logs  
* WPILib Data Logs (.wpilog)  
* CTRE Hoot Logs  
* Robot application logs  
* Coprocessor logs  
* Vision logs  
* Custom subsystem logs  
* Other team-defined diagnostic files

Logs shall be associated with the appropriate event, match, test run, or maintenance activity whenever this information can be determined.

---

## 3.2 Live Diagnostic View

The Live Diagnostic View shall provide real-time visibility into robot health while the robot is connected to the pit network.

The display shall support configurable dashboards containing metrics such as:

### Power

* Battery voltage  
* Battery current  
* Estimated power consumption  
* Voltage minimum / maximum  
* Voltage sag  
* Brownout events  
* Battery identifier  
* Battery state at beginning and end of test/match, when available

### CAN / Motor Controllers

* CAN bus utilization  
* CAN errors  
* CAN frame errors  
* Device connectivity  
* Motor controller faults  
* Motor controller temperatures  
* Motor output/current  
* Device reset events

### Robot Performance

* Loop timing  
* Loop overruns  
* CPU utilization  
* Memory utilization  
* Robot mode  
* Command/subsystem state  
* Brownout state  
* Network connectivity  
* Packet loss  
* Latency

### Drivetrain / Swerve

* Module angles  
* Module target angles  
* Steering error  
* Drive velocity  
* Drive current  
* Module temperature  
* Gyro heading  
* Gyro rate  
* Odometry status

### Subsystems

The application shall support team-defined, robot specific subsystem metrics, such as:

* Shooter velocity  
* Shooter current  
* Intake velocity/current  
* Mechanism positions  
* Climber position/current  
* Sensor states  
* Limit switch states  
* Encoder values  
* Control-loop errors

The system shall not require the application developer to hard-code every subsystem metric.

---

## 3.3 Log Review & Historical Diagnostics

The Log Review interface shall allow a user to select a previously recorded match, test, or log file and inspect robot behavior over time.

The interface shall provide a synchronized timeline for diagnostic data.

Users shall be able to:

* Play through the log chronologically.  
* Pause and resume playback.  
* Scrub to a specific timestamp.  
* Zoom into specific portions of a match.  
* Overlay multiple signals.  
* Compare signals from different subsystems.  
* Display minimum, maximum, and average values.  
* Identify faults and events on the timeline.  
* Jump directly to logged errors or warnings.  
* Correlate robot events with match timestamps.

### Event Markers

The timeline shall support markers for events including:

* Brownout  
* CAN error  
* Motor controller fault  
* Sensor fault  
* Loop overrun  
* Network interruption  
* Robot enable/disable  
* Mode transition  
* Subsystem state change  
* Driver command  
* Automated test step  
* User-created annotation

### Match-Centric Review

A completed match shall provide a diagnostic summary showing relevant robot health information for that match.

This shall include, where available:

* Battery voltage profile  
* Minimum battery voltage  
* Maximum current  
* Brownout events  
* CAN health  
* Motor temperatures  
* Motor controller faults  
* Loop timing  
* Network health  
* Subsystem-specific health metrics  
* Faults occurring during the match

This information shall remain available after the robot returns to the pit and shall be associated with the match record.

---

## 3.4 Configurable Diagnostic Dashboards

The diagnostic interface shall allow authorized users to configure what information is displayed.

Users shall be able to select:

* Metrics  
* Graphs  
* Tables  
* Status indicators  
* Gauges  
* Event timelines  
* Numeric values  
* Warning/fault indicators

Dashboard configurations shall be saveable as named views.

Example views may include:

* **Pit Health**  
* **Drivetrain**  
* **Shooter**  
* **Electrical**  
* **Match Review**  
* **Controls Debug**  
* **Automated Test**  
* **Battery Health**

The same dashboard configuration shall be usable with both live data and historical log data whenever the required signals are available.

### Graph Configuration

Users shall be able to configure:

* Signals displayed  
* Axis assignments  
* Time range  
* Sampling/display resolution  
* Units  
* Scaling  
* Threshold lines  
* Warning limits  
* Fault limits  
* Event overlays

The system shall allow a user to save and reuse graph configurations.

---

## 3.5 Health Trending

The system shall retain historical test results and allow comparison between test runs.

Examples include tracking:

* Battery voltage sag over time  
* Motor temperature  
* Motor current  
* CAN utilization  
* Steering error  
* Shooter performance  
* Mechanism travel time  
* Sensor accuracy  
* Loop timing

The system shall be able to identify changes from a team's established baseline and flag configurable deviations.

---

## 3.6 Diagnostic Thresholds & Alerts

Diagnostic thresholds shall be configurable rather than permanently hard-coded.

Each metric may have:

* Informational threshold  
* Warning threshold  
* Critical threshold

The application shall clearly distinguish between:

* Measured abnormal behavior  
* Configured warning  
* Configured fault  
* Confirmed hardware/software fault  
  ---

## 3.7 Battery Health Tracking

Battery information shall be associated with robot matches and test runs.

The system shall record, when available:

* Battery ID  
* Resting voltage  
* Minimum match voltage  
* Voltage sag  
* Peak current  
* Test results  
* Matches used  
* Test runs performed  
* User observations  
* Battery replacement/retirement status

The application shall provide historical battery health review and allow battery performance to be correlated with match and robot diagnostic data.

### Future Battery Charger Integration

Automated battery charger monitoring and charger telemetry are considered a **future system upgrade**.

The architecture should therefore allow charger telemetry to be integrated later, but charger monitoring is **not required for the initial release**.

---

# 4\. Interactive Checklists & Maintenance Reports

## 4.1 Automated & Manual Checklists

Checklists shall be integrated with robot state and event timing where practical.

### Start-of-Day Checklist

Examples include:

* Robot mechanical inspection  
* Fastener inspection  
* Electrical inspection  
* Main breaker verification  
* Radio/network verification  
* Driver Station verification  
* Vision system verification  
* Battery charging equipment inspection  
* Spare parts and tools verification

### Pre-Match Checklist

Examples include:

* Confirm assigned battery  
* Record battery ID  
* Verify battery condition  
* Verify bumper attachment and color  
* Verify robot configuration  
* Perform required subsystem checks  
* Verify critical sensor states  
* Verify driver station connectivity  
* Confirm robot ready state  
* Release robot to queue

### Post-Match Checklist

Examples include:

* Record driver/operator feedback  
* Perform visual damage inspection  
* Check critical fasteners  
* Inspect drivetrain  
* Inspect mechanisms  
* Check electrical connections  
* Offload robot logs  
* Associate logs with match  
* Review diagnostic warnings  
* Record required repairs  
* Determine robot readiness state  
  ---

# 5\. High-Pressure Pit Organization

## 5.1 Pit Big-Screen Kiosk Mode

The kiosk shall provide a high-visibility operational summary intended to be viewed from across the pit.

### Primary Status

Large status indicator shall display the current state of the robot and pit:

IN PIT  
PENDING \[CHECKLIST\]  
ROBOT READY  
AWAY

### Kiosk Information

The display shall optionally show:

* Current match  
* Next match  
* Countdown timer  
* Current event phase  
* Robot readiness  
* Active repair  
* Active checklist  
* Battery currently installed  
* Diagnostic warnings  
* Automated test result  
* Assigned pit responsibilities

The information displayed shall be configurable so that the team can create different kiosk layouts for different event phases.

---

## 5.2 Smart Battery Management

Battery identification and health tracking shall be supported.

The initial system shall focus on:

* Battery identification  
* Battery assignment  
* Match history  
* Battery health  
* Voltage measurements  
* Test results  
* Battery lifecycle

Automated charger telemetry and charging-queue optimization are reserved for a future release.

---

## 5.3 Pit Inventory & Fastener Map

The inventory system shall support:

* Spare part tracking  
* Storage location  
* Quantity  
* Minimum stock level  
* Component compatibility  
* Replacement history  
* Part number  
* Supplier information  
* QR/barcode identification

The system shall allow a pit crew member to quickly search for a component and receive its physical storage location.

---

## 5.4 Driver Station & Automated Robot Test

The application shall support a robot side automated test and analyze the robot state to give a report.

The application shall:

1. Verify that the robot is connected.  
2. Verify that required systems are available.  
3. Start the configured test sequence.  
4. Display test progress.  
5. Collect diagnostic measurements.  
6. Identify failed or abnormal test steps.  
7. Generate a PASS / WARNING / FAIL result.  
8. Store the complete test results.  
9. Compare results against previous tests.  
10. Provide a concise summary suitable for pit crew use.

Detailed diagnostic information shall remain available to controls/electrical personnel.

---

# 6\. Technical & Non-Functional Requirements

## 6.1 Architecture & Network Reliability

The application shall use an architecture that supports operation without reliable Internet connectivity.

Requirements include:

* Local-first data storage.  
* Local network synchronization.  
* Automatic synchronization when external connectivity becomes available.  
* No dependency on cloud services for critical pit operations.  
* Local robot log ingestion.  
* Local live diagnostic monitoring.  
* Local test execution.  
* Automatic recovery from temporary network interruptions.  
* Persistent storage of match and diagnostic data.

The system should be designed so that a complete event can be operated using only the team's local network.

---

## 6.2 Data Model & Historical Association

Diagnostic and operational records should be associated whenever possible with:

* Event  
* Match  
* Robot  
* Battery  
* Test run  
* Checklist  
* Maintenance event  
* Component  
* User  
* Timestamp

This allows the team to answer questions such as:

* What happened to the robot during Match 42?  
* Which battery was installed?  
* Did the robot pass its pre-match test?  
* What warnings occurred during the match?  
* Did a motor temperature increase over the course of the event?  
* Was the same subsystem showing warnings before the eventual failure?  
* What repairs occurred between two test runs?  
* Did the repair return the measured performance to baseline?  
  ---

## 6.3 Configurable User Interface

The application shall allow users to configure diagnostic and operational displays without modifying the application source code.

Configuration should include:

* Dashboard layouts  
* Metrics  
* Graphs  
* Thresholds  
* Subsystems  
* Test sequences  
* Checklist items  
* Event milestones  
* Match preparation timing  
* Kiosk displays  
  ---
